aspect: The document works; the reading of it does not
description: Unlike the Iranian or Palestinian cases in the sibling datasets, the Mexican passport is not itself a broken instrument. What it triggers is a presumption about intent - see VIS-001 - rather than non-recognition.
energy_note: A good passport, read as a statement of intent.
notes: Deliberate contrast with assets/text/iran DOC-001 and assets/text/palestine, where the document itself fails.

aspect: Visa-free access is wide and hollow where it matters
description: Mexicans travel visa-free to much of Europe, Japan and South America. The single destination that matters most for family, work and money - the United States - is the one that requires the interview.
energy_note: Free to go almost everywhere except where his family is.

aspect: Renewal from abroad is its own problem
description: Consular appointments abroad are scarce, and an expiring passport abroad interacts with an expiring immigration status: the man may not be able to renew one without the other.
energy_note: Two documents, each requiring the other.

description: His passport takes him to Japan, Brazil, Germany and Turkey without asking anyone. It does not take him to the hospital in San Diego where his mother is. He has shown it at eleven borders and been refused at the only one that mattered.
energy_note: Eleven countries open, and the one with his mother closed.
